lead_developers: R2 Companies and Lagfin S.C.A.
public_subsidy_note: $28 million in TIF (LaSalle Central TIF district) approved to support the project.

name: Chicago Fire FC Stadium at The 78
lead_developers: Chicago Fire FC (owner Joe Mansueto)
public_subsidy_note: Stadium itself is privately funded; surrounding infrastructure at The 78 is supported by TIF/public dollars.
investment_note: $650M widely cited at the June 2025 unveiling; some outlets later reported ~$750M. This is a distinct privately funded project, separate from the excluded 'The 78' master development (Related Midwest) and the White Sox ballpark proposal on the same 62-acre site.
log_line: 22,000-seat soccer-specific stadium entirely privately financed by Fire owner Joe Mansueto, anchoring the south end of The 78 riverfront site; broke ground March 2026 for a 2028 MLS-season opening.

name: 400 Lake Shore Drive
lead_developers: Related Midwest
investment_note: $500M is the secured construction financing for the first (north) tower; the full two-tower buildout is larger. Related Midwest bought the Spire site out of bankruptcy in 2014; the current two-tower SOM plan was unveiled ~2022 with financing in 2024.
log_line: Two-tower luxury residential development (~1,135 units, 1.1M sf) rising on the long-dormant Chicago Spire hole where the river meets Lake Michigan; the 72-story north tower is under construction, opening ~2027.

name: Halsted Landing (Onni Group, Goose Island)
lead_developers: Onni Group
investment_note: Casino-adjacent. Filed revised $1.1B renderings in 2024; still in approvals/pre-construction as of 2026. Distinct from Onni's nearby Halsted Pointe.
log_line: $1.1B riverfront megaproject of ~2,500 apartments across four towers (up to 650 ft), plus retail, an amphitheater and a water-taxi stop, betting on the adjacent Bally's permanent casino.

name: Halsted Pointe (Onni Group, Goose Island)
lead_developers: Onni Group
investment_note: $220M is the Phase 1 financing secured in late 2024 ($50M Otera Capital loan + $170M refinancing of Onni's 200 N LaSalle office); the full multi-tower masterplan is substantially larger. Distinct site from Onni's Halsted Landing.
log_line: Multi-tower Goose Island masterplan (ultimately ~2,650 units, a 300-key hotel and retail) on the former Greyhound site; Phase 1's 46-story, 500-ft tower broke ground April 2026 for a ~2028 opening.

name: Advocate Health Care South Side Investment / New South Works Hospital
lead_developers: Advocate Health Care (Advocate Health)
public_subsidy_note: Advocate (private nonprofit health system) funds the investment; the broader South Works site redevelopment involves public land and infrastructure.
investment_note: $1B total: $300M new hospital + $500M ambulatory + $200M chronic-care/maternal/social. Announced December 2024. Sits on a separate portion of the South Works site from the excluded Illinois Quantum & Microelectronics Park.
log_line: $1B South Side health-equity investment anchored by a new $300M, 52-bed hospital on 23 acres of the former U.S. Steel South Works site (near 81st St) to replace aging Trinity Hospital, plus $500M in ambulatory care and $200M in chronic/maternal/social spending.

name: Northwestern Memorial Hospital New Patient/Cancer Tower (Streeterville)
lead_developers: Northwestern Memorial HealthCare
investment_note: Cost 'could approach $1 billion' per Northwestern once construction, equipment and other expenses are included; project in Illinois state (Certificate of Need) review as of 2025-2026, not yet under construction.
log_line: Proposed ~1.2M-sf hospital tower on the downtown Streeterville campus (278 med-surg + 36 ICU beds, five ORs, cancer care, imaging); full build-out could approach $1B, with construction eyed for 2027.

name: Ogden Commons (North Lawndale)
lead_developers: The Habitat Company (with Sinai Health System)
public_subsidy_note: Opportunity Zone project on former CHA land with City of Chicago participation and TIF; substantial affordable-housing component.
investment_note: Phased. Phase 1 (commercial) completed 2021; Phase 2 (OC Living residential) secured financing 2023-2024 and is under construction. Habitat is the private master developer; partners include Sinai Health System, Alecko Capital and the City.
log_line: $200M, 10-acre mixed-use, mixed-income redevelopment of vacant CHA land in North Lawndale — billed as Chicago's largest Opportunity Zone project — delivering 350+ homes plus retail and Sinai health uses across multiple phases.

name: Salesforce Tower Chicago (Wolf Point South)
lead_developers: Hines (with Joseph P. Kennedy Enterprises)
investment_note: ~$800M construction cost; secured a $500M+ construction loan (later reported near a $610M refinancing). Announced 2018, completed and opened 2023-24.
log_line: 60-story, ~1.2M-sf riverfront office tower anchored by Salesforce, the third phase of the Wolf Point development at the Chicago River's main branch; opened 2023-2024.

name: One Chicago
lead_developers: JDL Development
investment_note: Announced and broke ground 2019; opened 2022. As of early 2026 JDL was shifting strategy to finish selling remaining raw condo units.
log_line: $850M two-tower River North mixed-use complex (76- and 49-story) with 735 apartments, 77 condos, a Whole Foods and Life Time fitness; completed 2022.

name: 1000M
lead_developers: Time Equities (with JK Equities and Oak Capitals)
investment_note: $470M project. Originally a 2016-era condo plan; after Goldman Sachs pulled funding in 2020 it was recapitalized and reworked as apartments, with construction restarting in 2020 and delivery in 2024.
log_line: 73-story, 738-unit luxury rental tower on South Michigan Avenue across from Grant Park — Helmut Jahn's final Chicago skyscraper; restarted in 2020 after a pandemic funding pause and opened June 2024.

name: Fulton Labs (Trammell Crow life-sciences campus)
lead_developers: Trammell Crow Company
investment_note: $220M is the 16-story 400 N Aberdeen building (~423,000 sf); the two-building Fulton Labs campus is larger. Trammell Crow spent $100M+ assembling the sites.
log_line: Fulton Market's first purpose-built life-sciences campus — a pair of lab/office buildings at 400 N Aberdeen and 1375 W Fulton totaling 700,000+ sf — anchoring the neighborhood's biotech pivot; completed ~2023.

name: Bank of America Tower (110 North Wacker)
lead_developers: Riverside Investment & Development and Howard Hughes Corporation
investment_note: Howard Hughes stated ~$722M build cost (2018 permit filings had estimated ~$300M). Opened 2020; later scored a $559M loan from anchor tenant Bank of America and sold down equity stakes.
log_line: 57-story riverfront office tower anchored by Bank of America, replacing the old Morton Salt building on Wacker Drive; opened late 2020 at a developer-stated ~$722M cost.
